titulo: Phrasal Verbs, Collocation and Register Shift
descripcion: At C2 the register ladder from look into to investigate to conduct an inquiry into extends further: the writer can shift register mid-text on purpose, dropping into the informal end for rhetorical effect within an otherwise formal piece, and knows exactly how far that shift can go before it breaks the whole register.

filas: reads as a slip, not a choice
can read as flat if never varied

ejemplos.texto: The committee conducted a thorough review — and, frankly, found a mess.
It's a great pub, though I should note it lacks any semblance of a wine list.
The report found nothing; in plainer terms, the whole exercise was wasted.

notas: A single deliberate register shift, well placed, reads as control and personality; two or more in the same short text reads as inconsistency.
The shift works best right after a formal or technical passage, where the contrast is sharpest.
In plainer terms and frankly are useful, controlled bridges from formal to informal register.

es.en: Formal Spanish tolerates a deliberate change of register within one text less than contemporary English, where a single well-placed informal turn counts as style rather than carelessness. Spanish speakers at C2 therefore tend to avoid register shifts altogether and lose a rhetorical tool professional English expects.
es.es: El español formal tolera menos que el inglés contemporáneo un cambio deliberado de registro dentro del mismo texto, donde un giro informal bien colocado se considera estilo y no descuido. Por eso, los hispanohablantes de C2 tienden a evitar por completo los cambios de registro y pierden una herramienta retórica habitual en el inglés profesional.

de.en: Separable verbs give German speakers a structural feel for phrasal verbs, so the forms themselves are easy. What is less familiar is the deliberate drop into informal register within a formal text, which German professional writing generally avoids, so German speakers keep the whole piece at the Latinate end.
de.de: Trennbare Verben geben Deutschsprachigen ein strukturelles Gefühl für «phrasal verbs», daher sind die Formen selbst leicht. Weniger vertraut ist der bewusste Wechsel in ein informelleres Register innerhalb eines formellen Textes, den deutsche Fachsprache meist vermeidet. Deutschsprachige bleiben daher oft durchgehend am lateinisch-formellen Ende.

it.en: Because Latinate English verbs are transparent to Italian speakers (investigate – «investigare»), the formal end of the register ladder feels safest. The deliberate drop into a phrasal verb for rhetorical effect is less familiar, as formal Italian tends to stay at one register throughout a text.
it.it: Poiché i verbi inglesi di origine latina sono trasparenti per gli italofoni («investigate» – «investigare»), il polo formale della scala di registro sembra il più sicuro. Il passaggio deliberato a un «phrasal verb» per effetto retorico è meno familiare, perché l'italiano formale tende a mantenere un unico registro per tutto il testo.

fr.en: Latinate English verbs are transparent to French speakers (investigate – «enquêter, investiguer»), and formal French writing keeps a stable, carefully policed register. French speakers therefore stay at the formal end and rarely risk a deliberate informal turn in English.
fr.fr: Les verbes anglais d'origine latine sont transparents pour les francophones («investigate» – «enquêter, investiguer»), et le français formel maintient un registre stable et très contrôlé. Les francophones restent donc au pôle formel et osent rarement un virage volontairement informel en anglais.

pt.en: Latinate English verbs are transparent to Portuguese speakers (investigate – «investigar»), so the formal end of the ladder feels safest. The deliberate informal turn within a formal text is less common in Portuguese professional writing and has to be practised as a conscious stylistic choice.
pt.pt: Verbos ingleses de origem latina são transparentes para falantes de português («investigate» – «investigar»), então o extremo formal da escala parece mais seguro. A virada deliberadamente informal dentro de um texto formal é menos comum na escrita profissional em português e precisa ser praticada como escolha estilística consciente.

errores: Shifting register more than once in a short text, which breaks consistency instead of adding effect.
Placing the informal shift somewhere it isn't set up by a preceding formal passage.
Avoiding any register shift at all, which reads as flat in a genre that expects some variation.

es: Defaulting to the Latinate cognate (*commence*, *terminate*, *obtain*) because it matches Spanish, which makes neutral prose sound stiff.
de: Calquing German separable verbs as phrasal verbs: *make on the light* from «*das Licht anmachen*» instead of *turn on the light*.
it: Defaulting to the Latinate cognate (*commence*, *terminate*, *obtain*) because it matches Italian, which makes neutral prose sound stiff.
fr: Defaulting to the Latinate cognate (*commence*, *terminate*, *obtain*) because it matches French, which makes neutral prose sound stiff.
pt: Defaulting to the Latinate cognate (*commence*, *terminate*, *obtain*) because it matches Portuguese, which makes neutral prose sound stiff.

mision.consigna: Write about caring for ageing parents, moving between conversational and academic register on purpose.
requisitos: three register ladders (phrasal → Latinate → fixed collocation)
one deliberate drop into plain speech in an otherwise formal paragraph

microtareas.texto: Build the ladder for *look after*, *take on* and *put up with*.
Write about *emotional labour* in academic register, then drop once.

autochequeo: Is there at most one deliberate register shift in a short text?
Is the shift set up by the surrounding register, not jarring?
Does the shift add effect rather than read as an accident?
Would an expert reader sense authorial control here?
Does the text also have a genre-appropriate baseline register, not just the shift?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on deliberate register shifts. Check that there's at most one, and that it's set up by the surrounding text rather than jarring. Do not rewrite the text.
